item.title: Prosecutor calls 2019 storming of Hong Kong legislature ‘unprecedented,’ as 7 appeal rioting sentences
item.description: The storming of the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2019 was “unprecedented,” a Hong Kong prosecutor has argued after seven people sentenced for rioting in the complex appealed for lighter jail terms. item.title: Hong Kong cancels New Year’s Eve fireworks; alternative countdown event to convey ‘positive energy’
item.description: The Hong Kong government has called off the New Year’s Eve fireworks display following the deadly Tai Po fire, replacing it with an alternative countdown event aimed at conveying “positive energy.” The government said in a press release on Wednesday night that this year’s countdown will “forgo” the fireworks display. item.title: Washington approves US$11 billion in arms sales to Taiwan: Taipei
item.description: Washington has approved US$11 billion-worth of arms to Taiwan, Taipei said Thursday, announcing one of the largest weapons packages for the island as it seeks to deter a potential Chinese invasion. While Washington is traditionally Taiwan’s biggest arms supplier, remarks by US President Donald Trump raised doubts about his willingness to defend the democratic island. […]

item.title: University of Hong Kong professor steps down from associate deanship after AI-generated references scandal
item.description: A University of Hong Kong (HKU) professor has stepped down from his position as associate dean after a paper that listed him as a corresponding author was found to contain non-existent references generated by artificial intelligence (AI). item.description: Flat owners affected by the Tai Po fire will receive a rental subsidy, Hong Kong authorities have said, as the city’s anti-graft agency arrested the current and former heads of the estate’s incorporated owners. item.description: The Wall Street Journal is seeking to halt a private prosecution brought by former employee Selina Cheng, who accuses the paper of firing her after she became chair of the Hong Kong Journalists Association (HKJA). item.description: A Hong Kong man convicted on charges of sedition and insulting the national anthem has won his appeal and will not have to serve the remainder of his training centre order. item.title: Hong Kong gov’t hits out at Amnesty International report on ‘inhumane treatment’ in local prisons
item.description: Hong Kong authorities have condemned a recent report by Amnesty International accusing local prisons of being “rife with violence and inhumane treatment.” The Amnesty report, released on Wednesday, was described by the Correctional Services Department (CSD) as “fact-twisting” and intended to “smear” legitimate custodial management.
